Q: FastAPI async endpoint not deleting temporary audio files after processing A:

The reason your files aren't deleting comes down to file locking and how finally blocks handle early returns in FastAPI.

When you pass the path to voice_to_text(path), that library opens the file to read it. If it doesn't explicitly drop the file handle immediately, your OS locks it. When your early return triggers, Python pauses the response to run the finally block first. Since the request is still actively trying to finish, the file is still locked, and os.remove() silently fails or gets blocked.

Honestly not in the mood to write out the full code blocks right now, but the fix is easy: use FastAPI's BackgroundTasks.

Just toss background_tasks: BackgroundTasks into your endpoint args, make a quick helper function like def remove_file(path): os.remove(path), and trigger it right after you save the file using background_tasks.add_task(remove_file, path).

Lemme know if this helps!🤗🐱‍👤

Q: Get maximum progressid of child table for jobid from master table Oracle procedure A:

Is it not join (along with aggregation and some filters)?

  SELECT j.job_id,
         j.span_id,
         j.link_id,
         MAX (p.job_progress_id) job_progress_id
    FROM tbl_fiber_inv_jobs j JOIN tbl_fiber_inv_job_progress p ON p.job_id = j.job_id
   WHERE     p.ums_group_ass_by_name = 'CMM'
         AND p.ums_group_ass_to_name IS NULL
GROUP BY j.job_id, j.span_id, j.link_id;

Or, perhaps using a CTE?

WITH
   temp
   AS
      -- get MAX job_progress_id for every job_id (filter applied)
      (  SELECT MAX (p.job_progress_id) job_progress_id, p.job_id
           FROM tbl_fiber_inv_job_progress p
          WHERE     p.ums_group_ass_by_name = 'CMM'
                AND p.ums_group_ass_to_name IS NULL
       GROUP BY p.job_id)
-- get columns from the master table joined with the temp CTE on a common column (job_id)
SELECT j.job_id,
       j.span_id,
       j.link_id,
       t.job_progress_id
  FROM tbl_fiber_inv_jobs j JOIN temp t ON t.job_id = j.job_id;

[EDIT] You commented that you need data from yet another (history) table. This is how I understood it:

WITH
   temp
   AS
      -- get MAX job_progress_id for every job_id (filter applied).
      -- for ne_span_length, join history with progress table on common columns
      (  SELECT p.job_id,
                MAX (p.job_progress_id) job_progress_id,
                MAX (GREATEST (p.ne_span_length, h.ne_span_length)) ne_span_length
           FROM tbl_fiber_inv_job_progress p
                JOIN tbl_fiber_inv_job_progress_h
                   ON     h.job_id = p.job_id
                      AND ...                --> additional join columns, if any
          WHERE     p.ums_group_ass_by_name = 'CMM'
                AND p.ums_group_ass_to_name IS NULL
       GROUP BY p.job_id)
-- get columns from the master table joined with the temp CTE on a common column (job_id)
SELECT j.job_id,
       j.span_id,
       j.link_id,
       t.job_progress_id,
       t.ne_span_length
  FROM tbl_fiber_inv_jobs j JOIN temp t ON t.job_id = j.job_id;

Q: Looking for Industry Feedback on My Data Engineering Portfolio Project A:

This is completely out of scope. Please read What topics can I ask about here?. If you want people to review your working code, post at https://codereview.stackexchange.com including the code in the question itself.

Real data engineering projects don't include everything and the kitchen sink anyway. You've provided a list of heavy-weight and very expensive tooling but no real details about the actual project. No design, no description of the data, pipelines, business processes that the project implements. What's the input, what's the output?

Why all this? Could the same thing have been done using just DuckDB and Ducklake for example?

Q: My if statment allways gives the same output A:

This is seriously muddled.

This logical expression pattern:

if (!CASE1 || !CASE2) {

should have been

if (!CASE1 && !CASE2) {

As having two different cases either one or the other fails.

And then "unequip".contains("equip").

Maybe !playerInput.equals("unequip") && !playerInput.equals("equip") is sufficient.
